title: Scientific Research Finding
description: A scientific finding is a result that survived method: observation, hypothesis, controlled test, statistical analysis, peer review. Example: 'mRNA vaccines showed 95% efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19 in phase-3 trials (Polack et al., NEJM 2020).' Its strength is the method section — anyone can check the work — and its honest companion is the limitations paragraph.

title: Audit Finding
description: An audit finding states a control gap with evidence: criteria (what should be), condition (what is), cause, and effect — plus a recommendation. Example: 'Payroll lacked segregation of duties: the same employee entered and approved 214 timesheets ($1.2M), violating policy FIN-114.' GAO's Yellow Book sets the standard; findings are rated by risk, not by embarrassment.

title: Archaeological Finding
description: An archaeological finding is context made legible: 'the hearth dates to 12,400 BCE (radiocarbon), with wheat phytoliths — among the earliest cooking evidence.' Stratigraphy gives relative order, radiocarbon and dendrochronology give absolute dates, and association — what lay with what — gives meaning. A pot shard without context is a rock; with context, it's a finding.
